audit_findings.title: The anchor and bridge use different post-transaction perimeters
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-transaction FY2025 OE anchor is projected against a post-acquisition and post-divestiture balance-sheet bridge, affecting OE, sustaining investment, interest expense and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Unless expressly stated otherwise, the operating and financial information presented in this Annual Report on Form 10-K does not give effect to the HG Acquisition or the Utica Shale Divestiture.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error. The $437.5 million anchor excludes HG and retains Utica operations, while the June 2026 bridge follows the $1.103052 billion HG acquisition and approximately $380 million net Utica proceeds. Direction is mixed because HG adds earnings and capital needs while Utica earnings and capital needs disappear. Transactions of this scale are reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE on the June 2026 perimeter using HG results from closing, removal of Utica results, normalized sustaining investment and the corresponding post-close financing costs; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Post-close acquisition interest may be absent from equity-level OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.8 million annualized pretax at June 2026 balances and rates, equal to 12.1% of the $437.5 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE DCF, recurring interest must reduce OE; the acquisition debt principal is not separately deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The HG Acquisition was funded with net proceeds of the 2034 Notes (as defined below), borrowing under the Credit Facility and restricted cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: FY2025 contains essentially none of a full year's HG financing cost. The $600 million 2034 notes at 5.75% imply $34.5 million annually, and the June revolver balance of $341.9 million at 5.35% implies another $18.3 million. The resulting $52.8 million pretax run rate is material relative to anchor OE, before fees and cash-tax effects.
audit_findings.action: Insert recurring interest, commitment fees, issuance-cost amortization and applicable cash-tax effects from the actual post-close capital structure into pro forma OE, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The unconsolidated stakes may be double counted
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings may remain in anchor OE while the underlying investments' $574.2 million value is also added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The gathering and processing segment also includes equity in earnings from the Company’s investments in the Joint Venture and Stonewall.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2025 income includes $116.439 million of equity-method earnings, but the supplied record does not establish whether those earnings or related distributions were purged when deriving the $437.5 million anchor. If they were not, the valuation counts both an earnings stream equal to 26.6% of anchor OE and a separate bridge asset equal to 8.5% of base equity value. That is reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Provide the line-by-line OE reconciliation. If equity-method economics remain in OE, either remove them and retain the $574.2 million stakes bridge or retain them in OE and remove the separate stakes value, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: Sustaining throughput may require capital classified as expansion
audit_findings.mechanism: Capital required to replace natural production decline should reduce OE as maintenance investment and may also reduce cash available to fund modeled growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Because of the natural decline in production from existing wells, our success depends, in part, on Antero Resources’ ability to replace declining production and our ability to secure new sources of natural gas from Antero Resources or third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated misclassification. The filing confirms that new connections offset natural decline and defines some well-connection spending as expansion, but it does not quantify the portion economically required merely to hold throughput and revenue flat. FY2025 total capital expenditures were $178.705 million, or 40.8% of anchor OE, so an unidentified sustaining component could matter, but the record cannot establish its size or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile capital spending by project to decline replacement, existing-capacity preservation and discretionary growth; normalize the first category as maintenance capital and rerun OE and growth funding.

audit_findings.title: The terminal period begins near key contract expirations
audit_findings.mechanism: Renewal pricing, volumes, commitments, termination rights and reinvestment after 2035-2038 affect terminal cash flows and the 2.5% terminal-growth assumption.
audit_findings.evidence: We have agreements in place to provide gathering and compression services through 2038 and water services through 2035.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking contract-renewal risk rather than a demonstrated error in current OE. The water agreement's initial term ends in 2035 and the principal gathering agreement's initial term ends in 2038, while terminal value supplies 47.7%-50.9% of operating PV. Carrying current economics through those dates could materially overstate value if renewal terms or volumes weaken, but present filings do not establish that they will.
audit_findings.action: Monitor amendments and renewal evidence, and before relying on the terminal value run explicit post-2035 and post-2038 downside cases for pricing, volumes, minimum commitments and sustaining capital.

audit_findings.title: The preferred claim is not fully reconciled to the common-share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.06875 million including liquidation preference and filed arrears, or approximately $0.021 per common share; recurring dividends are $0.55 million annually
audit_findings.mechanism: Any senior preferred amount not represented by common-equivalent shares should be deducted in the equity bridge, while recurring preferred dividends should reduce common OE without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: The Series A Preferred Stock ranks senior to the Company’s common stock as to dividend rights, as well as with respect to rights upon liquidation, winding-up or dissolution of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The reconciliation gap is real, but its filed scale cannot change the valuation conclusion. The $10 million liquidation preference plus $68,750 of arrears equals about 0.15% of the $6.721 billion base equity value and approximately $0.021 per share on 480.34 million shares. The $0.55 million annual preferred dividend is only 0.13% of anchor OE. These amounts are immaterial even if the existing dilution proxy does not capture the entire claim.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the exact conversion ratio and accrued-dividend balance, then replace the proxy with either exact if-converted shares or a preferred-claim deduction and dividend adjustment; no full valuation rerun is necessary unless the contractual claim materially exceeds the filed amounts.
